correctness.rationale: Independent small-order enumeration takes each possible clique size and each multiset of neighborhood subsets for the independent vertices, exhausting all unlabeled presentations up to reordering that independent set. Full atomic-pair color refinement with a shared palette and exact color-preserving isomorphism within each group reproduces 1,2,4,9,21,56,164 groups at orders 1–7, with no group containing nonisomorphic graphs; order zero is unique. Equal C² theories imply equality in every computed refinement round. At order eight the clique and independent set have degrees 5 and 2 and equitable quotient [[3,2],[2,0]], with four vertices per cell. The cross-incidence graphs are C₈ and 2C₄, so the pairs are equivalent but not isomorphic: any isomorphism must preserve the degree cells and hence the cross-incidence graph. The clique spans a connected component containing every independent vertex, making the graphs connected. After a join with K_t the degrees of the new, old-clique and old-independent vertices are respectively t+7, t+5 and t+2; the resulting equitable three-cell profiles agree and deleting the canonically identified new vertices recovers the original nonisomorphic pair. Counting cardinality handles different orders.
residual_risks: The frozen result concerns pairs inside the uncolored split class and does not enumerate all split collision classes at larger orders. The finite join tests do not prove the infinite claim; the degree and equitable-partition arguments do.

evidence: The chordal census claims no collisions for every chordal graph on 1–7 vertices and locates two doubletons at eight including the split pair.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Every split graph is chordal: an induced cycle of length at least four needs at least two clique vertices, and two clique vertices that are nonconsecutive or three clique vertices force a chord; two consecutive ones alone cannot make such a cycle through the independent set. Thus the broader finite separation includes split graphs.
